from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: The 'Language' of Coordinates", 
                          ["A basis is just our coordinate grid.", 
                           "Vectors are arrows, independent of grids.", 
                           "Different grids give different coordinate descriptions."])
        
        # Grid setup
        plane = NumberPlane(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.3})
        i_hat = Vector(RIGHT, color=YELLOW)
        j_hat = Vector(UP, color=BLUE)
        basis = VGroup(plane, i_hat, j_hat)
        
        v = Vector([1.5, 1], color=RED)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_in_area(basis, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(plane), GrowArrow(i_hat), GrowArrow(j_hat))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(GrowArrow(v))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(RED)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight coefficients (visual placeholder: Dot)
        dot_x = Dot(color=YELLOW).move_to(plane.c2p(1.5, 0))
        dot_y = Dot(color=BLUE).move_to(plane.c2p(0, 1))
        self.play(FadeIn(dot_x), FadeIn(dot_y))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Transition Matrix (The Bridge)", [
            "Define the transition matrix P.",
            "Columns are new basis in old.",
            "Equation: vector B equals P, vector C.",
            "P maps coordinates between bases.",
            "The bridge is built."
        ])
        
        # Colors for lines
        colors = [YELLOW, BLUE, GREEN, RED, ORANGE]

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(colors[0])
        matrix_p = MathTex("P = \\begin{pmatrix} [u]_B & [v]_B \\end{pmatrix}", font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_p, 'B3', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(matrix_p))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(colors[1])
        u_vec = MathTex("[u]_B = \\begin{pmatrix} 1 \\\\ 0 \\end{pmatrix}", color=BLUE, font_size=28)
        v_vec = MathTex("[v]_B = \\begin{pmatrix} 0 \\\\ 1 \\end{pmatrix}", color=GREEN, font_size=28)
        self.place_at_grid(u_vec, 'C2')
        self.place_at_grid(v_vec, 'C5')
        self.play(FadeIn(u_vec), FadeIn(v_vec))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(colors[2])
        equation = MathTex("[v]_B = P [v]_C", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(equation, 'D3', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(equation))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(colors[3])
        map_arrow = Arrow(start=self.grid['D3'], end=self.grid['E3'], color=RED)
        self.play(GrowArrow(map_arrow))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(colors[4])
        bridge_text = Text("Bridge Complete", color=ORANGE, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(bridge_text, 'E3')
        self.play(Write(bridge_text))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Identify new and old basis vectors.",
            "Construct the transition matrix P.",
            "Multiply P by new coordinates.",
            "Result is old coordinate vector.",
            "Calculation complete for basis change."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Step-by-Step Calculation", lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors for lines
        colors = [BLUE, GREEN, YELLOW, ORANGE, PURPLE]

        # Setup math objects
        matrix_p = MathTex(r"P = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{pmatrix}", font_size=36)
        vec_c = MathTex(r"v_C = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}", font_size=36)
        res_eq = MathTex(r"P v_C = v_B", font_size=36)
        
        # Elements to be shown
        eq_group = VGroup(matrix_p, vec_c, res_eq).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(colors[1])
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_p, "B2")
        self.play(FadeIn(matrix_p))

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Application & Summary", [
            "Simplifying transformations is our goal.",
            "Friendly bases make math easier.",
            "Example: switching to camera space."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show wireframe object
        wireframe = VGroup(
            Square(side_length=1.5, color=BLUE),
            Line(np.array([-0.75, -0.75, 0]), np.array([0.75, 0.75, 0]), color=BLUE),
            Line(np.array([-0.75, 0.75, 0]), np.array([0.75, -0.75, 0]), color=BLUE)
        )
        self.place_in_area(wireframe, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(wireframe))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Change camera perspective, updating object vertices via matrix
        self.play(Rotate(wireframe, angle=PI/4, about_point=wireframe.get_center()))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Display final rendered image
        render_result = Square(side_length=1.5, fill_opacity=1.0, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(render_result, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(render_result), FadeOut(wireframe))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: Change of Basis in Linear Algebra

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: The 'Language' of Coordinates
sections.content: Briefly define a basis as a set of 'coordinate axes' (vectors). A vector is just an arrow; its coordinates change based on the grid we draw behind it.
sections.example: Visual: A single arrow on a 2D plane. Show how it can be described by standard axes (x=1, y=2) versus a tilted, skewed grid.

sections.title: The Problem: Changing Perspectives
sections.content: Introduce the need to represent the same vector 'v' in two different bases, B and C. Explain that we need a bridge to translate coordinates from one system to another.
sections.example: Character: A drone flying in a room. The drone measures its position relative to the wall (Basis B), but the pilot measures it relative to their own position (Basis C).

sections.title: The Transition Matrix (The Bridge)
sections.content: Define the transition matrix P as the matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the new basis vectors expressed in the old basis. Formula: [v]_B = P * [v]_C.
sections.example: Animation: Show the basis vectors of C being 'decomposed' into the components of B. This mapping creates the columns of matrix P.

sections.title: Step-by-Step Calculation
sections.content: Demonstrate the algorithm: 1. Identify basis vectors, 2. Form matrix P, 3. Multiply P by new coordinates to recover old coordinates.
sections.example: Math: Let B = { (1,0), (0,1) } and C = { (1,1), (-1,1) }. Transition matrix P = [[1, -1], [1, 1]]. Transform point [1, 0]_C to [1, 1]_B.

sections.title: Real-World Application & Summary
sections.content: Conclude by showing why we do this: simplifying complex linear transformations (e.g., rotation/scaling) by choosing a 'friendlier' basis.
sections.example: Device: A game engine changing from 'World Space' (fixed map) to 'Camera Space' (what the player sees) to render 3D graphics efficiently.
